questions.q: Why are compliance NFRs treated differently from the other five NFR categories in this course?
options: Compliance NFRs are the least important category and can usually be deprioritized
Compliance NFRs are automatically satisfied by Salesforce's own platform certifications, with no customer-side work required

Compliance NFRs typically derive from a law, regulation, or contractual obligation already accepted by the business, so an architect generally doesn't get to negotiate them away the way they might trade off a performance target
Compliance NFRs only apply to government customers, not commercial ones
questions.explain: Unlike performance or scalability targets, which can often be traded off against cost or timeline, compliance NFRs usually stem from an already-accepted legal or contractual obligation, so the negotiation happens with legal/compliance stakeholders rather than inside the architecture trade-off process.

questions.q: Why is "Salesforce is compliant, so our org is compliant" a flawed assumption?
options: Because Salesforce's platform-level certifications describe its own infrastructure and shared responsibilities, not whether a specific customer's field-level security, sharing model, or integration design actually satisfies a given regulation for that org's specific use case
Because Salesforce has no compliance certifications at all
Because Salesforce certifications expire every 90 days and must be manually renewed by the customer
Because compliance only applies to on-premises systems, never to cloud platforms
questions.explain: Salesforce's certifications establish a compliant foundation for its own infrastructure, but a customer's specific implementation choices (which fields hold sensitive data, who can access them, retention, integration design) remain the customer's own compliance responsibility.

questions.q: Why is HIPAA described in this lesson as not being a certification Salesforce (or any vendor) can be directly awarded?
options: Because HIPAA only applies to hospitals, never to software vendors
Because HIPAA compliance is granted automatically to any company with ISO 27001 certification
Because HIPAA was replaced by GDPR for all U.S. companies

Because HIPAA is enforced through Business Associate Agreements and each covered entity's own compliance program, rather than a pass/fail audit of a platform — Salesforce instead supports HIPAA-relevant use cases through a HITRUST-audited report
questions.explain: HIPAA compliance is established through Business Associate Agreements and each covered entity's own program, not a certification a vendor earns outright. Salesforce supports HIPAA-relevant use cases via a HITRUST-audited report rather than claiming a direct 'HIPAA certification.'

questions.q: What does Salesforce's trust portal, compliance.salesforce.com, publish?
options: A live uptime dashboard with no certification information
Salesforce's compliance certifications and attestations, including programs like SOC 2/SOC 3, ISO 27001, and FedRAMP Moderate for Government Cloud
Customer-specific compliance audit results for each individual org
A directory of third-party AppExchange compliance consultants
questions.explain: compliance.salesforce.com is Salesforce's trust portal publishing its own compliance certifications and attestations, such as SOC 2/SOC 3 audit reports, ISO 27001 certification, and FedRAMP Moderate authorization specifically for Government Cloud.

questions.q: How should GDPR's Article 17 right to erasure be translated into an architectural NFR, per this lesson's approach?
options: As a policy statement only, with no required changes to data architecture
As a requirement to delete the entire Salesforce org upon any single erasure request

As a requirement that every object storing EU resident personal data support a documented deletion procedure covering the primary record and any copies in integrations, backups, and archives, within the regulation's required timeframe
As a requirement that applies only to Salesforce's own infrastructure, not customer-built integrations
questions.explain: Translating the right to erasure into a checkable design constraint means confirming that deletion actually reaches every copy of the data — primary records, integrated systems, backups, and archives — within the required timeframe, not just stating a policy intention.
